Use dsODN probes and ddPCR to find the optimal concentration of dsODN used for GUIDE-seq, and profile the off-target editing with the GUIDE-seq method.Note: Off-target is a common side effect from gene editing. GUIDE-seq (genome-wide, unbiased identification of DSBs enabled by sequencing) provides us with a genome-wide, unbiased, in vitro detection method to detect the off-target effect of living cells by sequencing.Note: an optimized GUIDE-seq method can be used in various cell types, such as primary human T cells including patient-specific variants, and is capable of identifying off-target cleavage/gene editing sites in a highly sensitive, unbiased, and genome-wide manner.41.Optimize the dsODN concentration.Note: GUIDE-seq requires the transfection of double-stranded oligodeoxynucleotide (dsODN) into cells. Considering that different cell types have different tolerances to dsODN, for example, high concentration of dsODN are required for certain transfection refractory cells, and low concentration are needed for many primary cells sensitive to cytotoxic from the dsODN, therefore, the concentration of dsODN must be optimized according to the cell type.Note: The blunt-ended dsODN used in our GUIDE-seq experiments was the same as used in the original GUIDE-seq paper (Tsai et al., 2015), and prepared by annealing (in the same way as annealing the Y adapter) two modified oligonucleotides of the following compositions:5ʹ- P-G∗T∗TTAATTGAGTTGTCATATGTTAATAACGGT∗A∗T -3ʹ and,5ʹ- P-A∗T∗ACCGTTATTAACATATGACAACTCAATTAA∗A∗C -3ʹ.(Where P represents a 5ʹ phosphorylation and ∗ indicates a phosphorothioate linkage.)Note: To optimize the dsODN concentration, two Affinity Plus (IDT) probes were designed for dsODN used in GUIDE-seq, and the sequences of the two probes are:dsODN probe-fwd: /5HEX/TT + G + A + G+TTG+T+CATATGT/3IABkFQ/ and,dsODN probe-rev: /5HEX/ACATATG+A+CAA+C+T + C + AA/3IABkFQ/,These two probes use “HEX” as the 5′ reporter dye and “Iowa Black FQ” as the 3′ Quencher. And “+” stands for locked nucleic acids which impart heightened structural stability, leading to increased hybridization melt temperature (Tm) of these two relatively short probes that targeted the central part of dsODN. Both forward and reverse probes work well in the ddPCR experiments.a.The dsODN concentration optimization steps start with testing the different amounts of dsODN in cells undergoing CRISPR-Cas9 editing.Note: For optimization of dsODN concentration, both the amount of dsODN added and the volume of the electroporation transfection buffer system need to be considered. In our experiment setting, the proper concentration of dsODN after the test is 1 μM (20pmol in 20 μL electroporation transfection buffer), while in the original paper [Tsai, S. et al. 2015], the concentration of dsODN used in U2OS cells is 5 μM (100pmol in 20 μL buffer), and in HEK293 cells is 0,25 μM (5pmol in 20 μL buffer).Note: first, the dsODN is provided at the amount ranging from about 1 pmol to about 10 nmol to the cells (the specific range depends on cell types) during electroporation (step 22–39), and the cell viability was monitored every day after the dsODN transfection until the samples are harvested.b.When editing fibroblast with Cas9 mRNA electroporation transfection (day-2), add the dsODN in wells which will be used as to check the off-target profile. dsODN should be added together with other reagents just before electroporation (step 32).c.A group of blank cells (blank control), a group of cells only with dsODN (background control) and a group of cells with editing but no dsODN (dsODN integration negative control) are included as three controls.Note: here is an example (Figure 2):Figure 2An example panel of experiment group designd.Next day, check the cell viability by taking aliquots for counting.Mix 10 μl Trypan Blue+10μl cells suspension and count with Countess. Record cell viability and amount of living cells/mL.Note: for Suspension cells, taking aliquots for counting is easy; and for adherent cells, cells need to be trypsinized into single cell suspension before counting, thus setting wells specifically be used for checking cell viability is strong recommended.e.Check and record cell viability in each condition every day until cells sample was harvested and draw cell viability curves accordingly.f.After sample harvested, the editing efficiency at that particular gene editing target is determined by ddPCR (according to the manual: ddPCR ™ HDR Genome Edit Detection Assays, 2017,https://www.bio-rad.com/sites/default/files/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/10000065281.pdf, ddPCR ™ NHEJ Genome Edit Detection Assays, 2017 https://www.bio-rad.com/sites/default/files/webroot/web/pdf/lsr/literature/10000065278.pdf, or other paper5).g.At the same time, the dsODN integration rate to that particular target site is also determined by ddPCR with the dsODN probes mentioned above.Note: The dsODN integration rate at the target editing sites can be regarded as a representative parameter for all dsODN integration rates in whole genome double strands break sites for there is a direct relationship between them.h.After we obtained the cell viability (from step 40-d,e), target site editing efficiency and target site dsODN integration rates (from step 40-f), we can then comprehensively consider and determine the optimal dsODN concentration for a specific cell type under specific conditions.42.GUIDE-seq sample steps.title: Prepare Y‑adapter for GUIDE‑seq
steps.instruction: Anneal the MiSeq common oligo with each sample barcode adapter (A01‑A16) in 1× TE buffer (80 µL) adding 10 µL 100 µM MiSeq Common Adapter_MI to a final volume of 100 µL; the adapters contain an 8‑mer NNWNNWNN index. Run the thermocycler program: 95 °C for 1 s, 60 °C for 1 s, then ramp down slowly (~‑2 °C/min) to 4 °C and hold. Store the annealed Y‑adapter at ‑20 °C (stable for ≥1 year).

steps.title: Purify Cas9 mRNA by LiCl precipitation
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL of 7.5 M LiCl, 50 mM EDTA solution to the 50 µL in‑vitro transcription reaction (final LiCl 2.5 M). Incubate at ‑20 °C for ≥30 min (overnight optional). Centrifuge at 4 °C, >12 000 rpm for 15 min. Remove supernatant, rinse pellet with 500 µL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, centrifuge 4 °C for 10 min. Remove ethanol, briefly spin to collect residual liquid and remove with a fine tip. Air‑dry the pellet for a few minutes (≤10 min). Resuspend mRNA in nuclease‑free water, aliquot into PCR tubes, label and store at ‑20 °C (<6 months) or ‑80 °C (>6 months).

steps.title: Electroporate fibroblasts with editing components
steps.instruction: Prepare cultured primary fibroblasts and mix in‑vitro transcribed Cas9 mRNA, sgRNA (not crRNA‑tracrRNA hybrids), and ssDNA repair template (and dsODN if performing GUIDE‑seq). Electroporate according to the cell‑type‑specific protocol (typically 4–5 h total). Recover cells in appropriate culture medium. Note: CleanCap‑capped mRNA may increase HDR efficiency.

steps.title: Optimize dsODN concentration for GUIDE‑seq
steps.instruction: Prepare blunt‑ended dsODN by annealing the two modified oligos (5ʹ‑P‑G*TTTAATTGAGTTGTCATATGTTAATAACGGT*A*‑3ʹ and 5ʹ‑P‑A*TC CGTTATTAACATATGACAACTCAATTAA*A*C‑3ʹ; * = phosphorothioate, P = 5ʹ‑phosphate). Design two Affinity Plus probes for ddPCR: dsODN probe‑fwd (/5HEX/TT+G+A+G+TTG+T+CATATGT/3IABkFQ/) and dsODN probe‑rev (/5HEX/ACATATG+A+CAA+C+T+ +C+AA/3IABkFQ/). Test a range of dsODN amounts (≈1 pmol to 10 nmol) added during electroporation (e.g., 20 pmol in 20 µL buffer = 1 µM, the concentration found optimal in this study). Include three controls: (1) blank cells, (2) cells receiving dsODN only, (3) cells edited without dsODN. The next day, assess viability by mixing 10 µL Trypan Blue with 10 µL cell suspension and counting with a Countess; for adherent cells, trypsinize before counting. Record viability daily until harvest. After harvest, determine target‑site editing efficiency by ddPCR (HDR or NHEJ assays) and dsODN integration rate at the target site using the dsODN probes. Use these data to select the optimal dsODN concentration (20–50 pmol in 20 µL buffer; 1 µM was chosen).

steps.title: Prepare GUIDE‑seq library from genomic DNA
steps.instruction:
Extract genomic DNA, assess purity (Nanodrop 260/280 ≈1.80, 260/230 ≈2.0) and quantify by Qubit. Dilute to 100 µL in 1× TE (1–20 ng/µL, 10 ng/µL recommended) in 0.65 mL Bioruptor tubes. Vortex 5–10 s, centrifuge 10 s, keep on ice 5–10 min. Shear to 400–500 bp using Bioruptor Pico: 7 cycles, 15 s ON / 90 s OFF at 4 °C. Optional: run 5 µL sheared DNA on 1.2 % agarose gel. Take 400 ng sheared DNA, bring to 120 µL with 1× TE, clean with 120 µL AMPure XP beads (1×), elute in 15 µL 1× TE.

End‑repair & A‑tailing (per reaction, total 22.5 µL): 1.5 µL H₂O, 1.0 µL 10× dNTP mix (5 mM), 2.5 µL 10× T4 DNA Ligation Buffer (NEB B0202S), 1.0 µL End‑repair Enzyme mix (Fast DNA End Repair Kit K0771), 2.0 µL Mg²⁺‑free Buffer for Taq Polymerase, 0.5 µL non‑hot‑start Taq Polymerase, 8.5 µL DNA sample, add water to 22.5 µL. Thermocycle: 12 °C 15 min, 37 °C 15 min, 72 °C 15 min, hold 4 °C.

Adapter ligation (per reaction, total 25.5 µL): 1.0 µL annealed Y‑adapter_MI (10 µM), 2.0 µL T4 DNA Ligase, 22.5 µL end‑repair product. Thermocycle: 16 °C 30 min, 22 °C 30 min, hold 4 °C. Clean with 0.9× (22.95 µL) AMPure XP beads, elute in 12 µL 1× TE.

PCR‑1 (30 µL total): 11.9 µL H₂O, 3.0 µL 10× Buffer for Taq Polymerase (Mg²⁺‑free), 0.6 µL dNTP mix (10 mM), 1.2 µL MgCl₂ (50 mM), 0.3 µL Platinum Taq (5 U/µL), 1.0 µL GSP1 primer (10 µM) or primer pool, 1.5 µL TMAC (0.5 M), 0.5 µL P5_1 (10 µM), 10.0 µL adapter‑ligated DNA. Use Discovery touchdown program (95 °C 5 min; 15 cycles 95 °C 30 s, anneal 70 °C → 56 °C (‑1 °C per cycle) 2 min, 72 °C 30 s; 10 cycles 95 °C 30 s, anneal 55 °C 1 min, 72 °C 30 s; 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C) or Validation program (95 °C 5 min; 14 cycles 95 °C 30 s, anneal ramp down 20 % to 65 °C, extension 65 °C 5 min; 72 °C 5 min; hold 4 °C). Clean with 1.2× (36 µL) AMPure XP beads, elute in 15 µL 1× TE.

PCR‑2 (30 µL total): 5.4 µL H₂O, 3.0 µL 10× Buffer for Taq Polymerase (Mg²⁺‑free), 0.6 µL dNTP mix (10 mM), 1.2 µL MgCl₂ (50 mM), 0.3 µL Platinum Taq (5 U/µL), 1.0 µL GSP2 primer (10 µM) or pool, 1.5 µL TMAC (0.5 M), 0.5 µL P5_2 (10 µM), 1.5 µL P7_# (10 µM; use at least four distinct indexes), 15.0 µL DNA from PCR‑1 cleanup. Apply the same thermocycler program as PCR‑1 (Discovery or Validation). Clean with 0.7× (21 µL) AMPure XP beads, elute in 30 µL 1× TE.

Library quantification: Quantify the final library by qPCR (e.g., Kapa Biosystems Illumina Library Quantification kit) following the manufacturer’s instructions and submit for Illumina sequencing.

steps.title: Count living cells daily during dsODN optimization
steps.instruction: Each day, take an aliquot of electroporated cells, mix 10 µL Trypan Blue with 10 µL cell suspension, and count live cells using a Countess cell counter (for suspension cells) or after trypsinization (for adherent cells). Record viability and live cell concentration (cells/mL). Plot viability curves and use the data together with ddPCR editing efficiency and dsODN integration rates to decide the optimal dsODN amount.
